title: Climate & finance
voice: Every title, desc, comment or intro here is read by a player and is written as Envie speaking. See CLAUDE.md and _DESIGNS/envie-voice-and-text-rewrite-guide.md: plain short sentences, no em-dashes, European spelling, no emoji, facts and sources untouched. The optional 'envie' line on a slide is his own aside, one short sentence.

slides.text: Your money has a carbon footprint. Time to have a word with your bank.
When people talk about climate, they talk about technology, policy and behaviour. There's another part that gets far less attention:
slides.envie: I never had a bank account up there.

slides.text: Both public and private money are needed to pay for the climate transition. No government can do it alone.
bullets: It's estimated $9.2 trillion a year is needed until 2050 to reach net zero (McKinsey)
Every $1 invested in climate resilience can return up to $4 in benefits (World Bank)
slides.footer: So why are some banks still funding the wrong projects?

slides.text: Your bank doesn't just hold your money. It uses it. Every euro you deposit is lent out, many times over. A big share goes to oil, gas and deforestation.
slides.footer: Up to 30% of lending in some banks. You don't see it. You don't sign off on it. But it happens every day.

slides.caption: €1,000 held in a carbon-heavy bank causes the same yearly emissions as a return flight from New York to Seattle. For most people, banking produces more indirect emissions than their flights.
slides.bold: flight from New York to Seattle
slides.envie: Your money works while you sleep. The question is for whom.

slides.caption: Put together, the 60 largest banks have given $3.8 trillion to fossil fuel companies since the Paris Agreement in 2015.
slides.note: While 29 of the 30 largest financiers had publicly committed to net zero.
slides.envie: Read that number again. I did.

slides.title: Time to check what kind of bank you give your money to.
bad: Net zero pledges not matched by action
good: No financing to fossil fuel expansion

slides.caption: Switch to a climate-responsible bank and you could cut the climate impact of your banking by 76%. One decision. No cost. No change to your daily life.
slides.note: Bigger impact than years of diet changes.

slides.text: The system is still funding the wrong things. You can choose which part of it you feed. Check your bank at bank.green or BankTrack. Switch once, benefit for years.
